applicable_semantics.rule: when storage_kind = latch, the elements A5FF, B5FF, C5FF, D5FF are not storage elements: their ff_init and ff_srval relations are not applicable (not unknown); sr_kind is not applicable to a latch (its SR is asynchronous)
applicable_semantics.status: a model assumption drawn from docs/ff_latch_probe.md; a changed context is not an illegal configuration

ce_mode.bit_one_means: CE driven from the slice input

sr_mode.bit_one_means: SR driven from the slice input

storage_kind.bit_one_means: latch (AFF..DFF are LDCE / LDPE; A5FF..D5FF are not storage elements)

initialisation_event.assumption: sets Q := INIT on every applicable element and clears nothing else; modelled on the UNISIM GSR

fields: ce, sr, d (one bit per element)
q_before, q_after per element (0 | 1 | null = not applicable or never initialised)
observation_context.status: every readout carries all of these; the stimulus sequence, the configuration and the initial state are part of the trace header

primitive_selection.rule: by (storage_kind, sr_kind, SRVAL): flip-flop + synchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDRE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDSE; flip-flop + asynchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDCE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDPE; latch + SRVAL 0 -> LDCE; latch + SRVAL 1 -> LDPE (a latch's SR is always asynchronous; sr_kind is not applicable to a latch)

scope: SLICE_X2Y25 (CLBLL_L_X2Y25, SLICEL_X0): the 21 addresses of the clb_ff_config class on that site, the eight storage elements of the slice. A model's definitions. Nothing here is a claim about silicon: no row below has been observed on a board (docs/b4_architecture.md section 4.4).

adopted: on the active edge of C (posedge; negedge when IS_C_INVERTED, lines 71-98): if R then Q <= 0 else if CE then Q <= D
R is synchronous: it acts only at the edge
as FDRE with the synchronous input S setting Q <= 1 at the edge (lines 75-82)
glblGSR asserted: Q_out = INIT; CLR_in asserted: Q_out = 0 at any time, level-sensitive (lines 72-80)
on the active edge of C with CLR_in low: if CE then Q <= D (lines 84-111)
as FDCE with the asynchronous input PRE setting Q_out = 1, level-sensitive (lines 72-76)
G_in = G xor IS_G_INVERTED; GE_in = GE (lines 63-71)

the UDP latchsre_ldce (lines 183-209): with set = rst = 0, q+ = d while clk = 1 and ge = 1 (transparent), q+ = q while clk = 0 or ge = 0 (hold); rst = 1 gives q+ = 0 and set = 1 gives q+ = 1 at any time
as LDCE with the asynchronous input PRE setting Q = 1 (lines 64-71)
which address each of the 22 mine-site feature names moves (21 distinct addresses; CLKINV and NOCLKINV share one)
the specimen pair of every feature, from which the direction of every bit reading below is taken

items: the pin correspondence: the slice clock is C (or G for a latch), CE is CE (or GE), SR is R / S / CLR / PRE by the decoded kind and value

the initialisation event of the carrier is modelled as the UNISIM GSR: every applicable element takes its INIT — whether the carrier's event does so on silicon is condition A8 of docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.5
sources.source: docs/ff_preregistration_plan.md section 2 (the Z polarity readings) and section 3 (the attestation fields); docs/ff_latch_probe.md (a slice holds four latches, on AFF..DFF); this project's own choice of how the seven semantics select a primitive and its parameters

valid_configuration.rule: every assignment of the 21 bits is in the model's domain
valid_configuration.status: a domain definition for the model (v0.1); not a statement that any configuration is legal to build, safe to write, or observed
